sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the export
sections.what: Loads the tools for building PowerPoint files, the scan data types, the chart builder, the schedule calculation and the slide adder.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the export tied to the shared chart and schedule rules.
sections.watch_out: Several imports reach up through long relative paths, so moving files breaks them.

sections.name: ScanExportChart, num
sections.title: Chart settings and a number helper
sections.what: Defines the chart settings the export accepts, and a helper that returns a field's value only when it is a finite number.
sections.why: Charts need real numbers, so anything else is treated as missing.
sections.watch_out: A stored value that is numeric text is treated as missing.

sections.name: toTemplateProject
sections.title: Converting a project for the template
sections.what: Reshapes one project's scan data into the layout the slide template needs. It attaches the source link and quote for budget and schedule figures and calculates a schedule overrun percentage.
sections.why: The template expects a fixed shape, and each figure must keep its source.
sections.watch_out: Only figures that have a source link keep a citation, so an uncited figure appears with no reference.

sections.name: require
sections.title: Loading the PowerPoint library
sections.what: Loads the PptxGenJS library through a Node-style loader so this module can use it.
sections.why: Likely reason: this module uses the modern module format, while the library uses the older format.
sections.watch_out: If the library is missing, the export fails only when this line runs.

sections.name: value
sections.title: Formatting a value with its unit
sections.what: Shows a stored value followed by an optional unit, or the text Not available when there is no value.
sections.why: Gives slides one consistent text for missing data.
sections.watch_out: Values are shown exactly as stored, with no rounding or formatting.

sections.name: renderScanExport (part 1)
sections.title: Building the deck and first slides
sections.what: Creates a new PowerPoint file in memory, sets its title and author, then adds a cover slide, a how-the-analysis-works slide, and a bubble chart slide for the chosen projects. It also keeps only the evidence quotes whose stored source text matches a displayed project field, so only those quotes can be cited.
sections.why: Likely reason: the export is a snapshot of stored facts, built on demand and never saved, and the matching filter keeps citations tied to real fields. The bubble chart note is cut off in the packet, so its full wording is unclear here.
sections.watch_out: Citations depend on an exact text match between the quote and the stored field, so a small change to either side silently drops the citation.

sections.name: renderScanExport: for
sections.title: Project, risk, strength and source slides
sections.what: Adds two slides per selected project, one with benchmark inputs and one with source coverage. Then it adds risk and strength slides in groups of five bullets, a conclusions slide, and one slide per cited quote, split into chunks of up to 1500 characters, each with a clickable link when the URL is valid.
sections.why: Likely reason: groups of five bullets and 1500-character chunks keep text readable and stop it running off the slide.
sections.watch_out: The bracketed reference numbers on project slides and quote slides both come from the same filtered quote list, so both must be built from that same list or the numbers will not match.

summary: Turns a scan's saved project data into a PowerPoint file, with citations for budget and schedule figures.
purpose: Creates the downloadable scan deck, including a bubble chart slide and the project figures.
why: Reason beyond the export feature not stated in the code. The code converts data into the shape the deck template expects.
how: Converts each project into the template format with its cited sources and calculates schedule overrun percentages. The rest of the rendering, which is not in this packet, builds slides with the PptxGenJS library and returns the file bytes.
inputs: Project scan data, saved evidence quotes, the synthesis result and optional chart settings.
outputs: The bytes of a PowerPoint file.
risks: Only part of this file was provided, so the full rendering logic is not confirmed. Missing values become the text Not available, which could be mistaken for real data. The library is loaded at run time, so a missing install fails only when the export runs.
debug: If the file will not open, check the export function and the library installation. If citations are missing, check the citation step for empty source addresses. If the chart is wrong, check the chart settings and the chosen project subset.
